sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Democrats won control of the House and Senate in the US midterms. Voters supported 40 of 41 ballot measures restricting data centre development. Meanwhile, Republican Senator Ted Cruz scheduled a hearing for Danielle Thumann Severs to secure a Republican majority on the Federal Communications Commission.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The results reflected strong public opposition to rapid AI expansion, prompting a selloff in tech stocks. Focus on economic pressures like tariffs enabled Democrats to flip seats in traditionally Republican states.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: King Charles III led senior members of the Royal Family at the annual Royal British Legion Festival of Remembrance at London's Royal Albert Hall. The Prince of Wales, Catherine, Princess of Wales, and Queen Camilla attended alongside veterans, serving personnel, and bereaved families. Hosted by Clive Myrie, the event included musical performances and commemorated those lost in service. It also marked conflict anniversaries. Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Defence Secretary Wes Streeting were present.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The festival honours British service personnel who lost their lives in service. Prime Minister Andy Burnham noted that Remembrance Sunday provides an opportunity to reflect on the selflessness, courage, and sacrifice required to protect others.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: On Remembrance Sunday, the King will lead a two-minute silence and lay wreaths at the Cenotaph in central London. He will be joined by senior royals and political leaders, with 10,000 veterans joining the march-past.

gist: The UK spent at least £100m on unused zombie Brexit border inspection posts.
Sites were built and quickly decommissioned as plans for checks changed.
Ports and local councils now face high costs and uncertainty.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The UK spent at least £100m on seven inland border facilities that were never used or quickly decommissioned. Sites in places like Birmingham, Ebbsfleet, North Weald, Warrington and Dover were built or planned as the government vacillated over post-Brexit checks on EU goods, before most checks were scaled back.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The expenditure wasted millions in taxpayers money on redundant infrastructure. Local councils and ports, such as Portsmouth which spent £23m on an underused facility, were left with funding shortfalls and uncertain futures for bespoke buildings that now face costly demolition or repurposing.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Ports and local leaders are calling on the government to provide compensation for the redundant border posts as future border arrangements with the EU come into force.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: While shopping in Ikea to distract herself from difficult dating experiences, a widowed woman became overwhelmed by seeing couples and families. Sitting on a display sofa, she burst into tears. A passing woman stopped, handed her a packet of tissues, placed a hand on her shoulder, and walked away after she felt better.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The silent gesture broke the woman's sense of deep isolation, reminding her that new human connections were possible. It restored her belief in finding a relationship and inspired her to carry tissues to help others in similar distress.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The woman met a wonderful new man and has been with him for over a decade. She now carries travel tissues in her purse and has helped crying strangers on four separate occasions.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Hair stylist and businessman John Frieda died at the age of 75. He began his career in the 1960s, working in Leonard Lewis’s London salon before opening his own venue in New Cavendish Street in 1976. He styled numerous famous figures and later partnered with Gail Federici to launch commercial haircare products, including the famous Frizz Ease range, before selling the company in 2002.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Frieda was a pioneer who changed the direction of hair aesthetics from fixed, helmet-like styles to natural-looking, manageable hair that respected individual textures like curls and kinks. His innovations, particularly the creation of anti-frizz serum, shifted the industry and created a major global retail market.

Tuesday briefing: The world is falling short on climate action. Can Cop31 change that?

gist: COP31 climate talks have opened in Antalya, Turkey, amidst warnings of record temperatures.
Scientists predict 2026 will be among the warmest years ever recorded.
Expanding greenhouse gases and El Niño accelerate global heat accumulation and extreme weather.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: World leaders gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for the COP31 climate summit as scientists warned 2026 is on track to be one of the warmest years on record. Berkeley Earth predicts 2026 will break records, whilst the WMO forecasts it among the top four warmest years.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Global heating is accelerating due to carbon dioxide emissions and a powerful El Niño. Extreme weather events like wildfires in Europe and deadly glacier collapses in Nepal highlight rising human costs. Ocean heat and sea levels have reached record highs, making warming irreversible on centennial timescales.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: El Niño is forecast to continue into 2027, maintaining high temperatures. Research suggests Earth could permanently cross the 1.5C limit in 2028. Governments at COP31 are discussing climate goals, funding adaptation, and AI energy demands, though some nations are reducing aid and EV targets.

timeline.text: The climate case for AI has not been made

gist: AI is frequently touted as a major climate solution.
Major industries have been slow to adopt AI for climate goals.
AI data centers are increasing emissions and energy consumption.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey for a climate conference where artificial intelligence was a central topic. While companies have made bold predictions about AI fixing the climate or reducing global emissions, reviews of major sectors show that few industries have actually adopted the specific emissions-reducing applications envisioned by researchers.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Projections about AI cutting billions of tons of emissions remain largely aspirational. Furthermore, the rapid growth of data centers is driving up energy use and emissions, causing major tech firms to fall behind on their environmental targets.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Private BitTorrent trackers operate as exclusive, invite-only communities where users share and curate vast catalogues of pirated media. Members adhere to strict community rules, maintaining upload-to-download ratios by seeding content to gain rank and access to more exclusive servers. Some users actively seek out long-lost or rare media, such as unpublished literary works and obscure documentaries, to upload and preserve them.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Supporters and researchers argue that private trackers act as digital archives preserving cultural material absent from commercial streaming platforms. However, copyright enforcement bodies like the Motion Picture Association view private trackers as illegal operations that feed broader unauthorized distribution networks.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Rightsholders continue to investigate and target private trackers, their administrators, and supporting infrastructure, maintaining that closed communities remain vulnerable to legal enforcement.

timeline.text: ‘A medieval jigsaw puzzle’: rediscovering Coventry cathedral’s ‘stunning’ stained glass windows

gist: Coventry cathedral has catalogued thousands of medieval stained glass fragments for digital access.
The 15th-century glass, attributed to John Thornton, survived the Reformation and second world war.
The scanned collection is available to view via the Bloomberg Connects app.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Thousands of 15th-century stained glass fragments from Coventry cathedral have been catalogued and photographed. Packed into 30 wooden crates following 1940 Luftwaffe bombing, the remnants survived both the Reformation and the second world war. Led by stained glass conservator Laura Atkinson, the project offers virtual public access to the collection.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts consider the glass, attributed to master glazier John Thornton, to be an internationally significant treasure trove. The fragments depict biblical scenes, donors, animals and intricate jewels, showcasing high-end medieval craftsmanship. Digital access allows researchers to study glassmaking techniques, track medieval craftspeople, and potentially use AI to reconstruct original window designs.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The scanned glass collections are available for public browsing on the Bloomberg Connects app during November. Coventry cathedral plans to establish a permanent digital archive in the future.

quotes.text: It is the faces that obviously really capture you.

gist: A woman trained her black labrador, Mae, as a medical alert dog.
Mae smells oncoming medical episodes and alerts her owner to prevent injuries.
Mae helped her owner manage her health and complete her cancer research PhD.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In 2023, an owner with multiple health conditions acquired Mae, an 11-week-old black labrador. Due to long waiting lists for assistance animals, she trained Mae as a medical alert dog with help from the charity Medical Detection Dogs. Mae recognises changes in her owner's odour when a medical episode is approaching and alerts her by staring intensely or jumping gently.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Mae's alerts prevent her owner from falling and injuring herself when passing out alone. With Mae's support, her owner resumed horse riding and independent driving, completed an eight-year PhD in cancer research, and dramatically reduced anxiety for both herself and her family.

gist: A Sunderland councillor was convicted over a Facebook post concerning Nigerian people.
The official claimed the remarks were a joke, but a judge disagreed.
A community order and unpaid work were handed down, and an appeal is planned.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Glenn Gibbins posted a message on Facebook stating that Nigerian people in town should be melted to fix potholes. After being elected in Sunderland, the post emerged, leading to a trial at South Tyneside Magistrates Court. District Judge Zoe Passfield found him guilty of sending a grossly offensive communication, handing him a community order with unpaid work. His legal team stated they intend to appeal.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The prosecution argued that the remarks diminished human life and conjured historical atrocities, causing distress among local residents. The defense argued the statement was merely an unpolitical, foolish joke and highlighted free speech concerns, while the judge ruled the language specifically targeted an ethnic minority.

timeline.text: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity

gist: Data center backlash is primarily driven by massive electricity consumption rather than just culture wars.
Virginia facilities draw grid power while rural AI centers require massive onsite natural gas generation.
Developers may target sparse areas like the Permian Basin, abroad, or space to avoid resistance.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Data center hubs like Ashburn, Virginia, have seen growing public backlash. While Big Tech frames this as a proxy culture war over corporate power and affordability, activists and developers note the opposition is fundamentally about electricity consumption and grid strain.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: AI data centers require unprecedented power capacity, ranging from 300 to 6,000 megawatts. Connecting to local grids strains resources and risks increased fossil fuel use, while generating power onsite using natural-gas turbines or diesel backup releases air pollutants in surrounding communities.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: New data centers needing onsite power may relocate to sparsely populated regions with natural gas networks like the Permian Basin, expand abroad such as Google in Malaysia, or potentially look to space.

fivew: Big Tech companies, activists like Elena Schlossberg, and local communities.
Public backlash against data centers is driven by their massive electricity consumption and physical impact.
Data Center Alley in Ashburn, Virginia, and rural areas across the US.
AI and data centers demand unprecedented amounts of electricity from the grid or onsite generators.

gist: A vulnerability allowing hackers to SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation.
Multiple security firms report exploitation activity linked to botnets and cryptocurrency.
Users of OpenSSH and musl should install updates and investigate further promptly.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Security firms reported exploitation activity related to botnets and cryptocurrency targeting a vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-123158. The flaw resides in OpenSSH running alongside musl without PAM, requiring specific password configurations. Exploits occur when attackers enter passwords with more than 256 characters for passwordless accounts, causing errors in password hashing.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Despite multiple necessary conditions, the vulnerability poses a serious threat to a large base of machines, particularly those running the Alpine Linux distribution. Millions of exposed SSH servers can be tested for vulnerabilities in seconds.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Anyone using OpenSSH should install the update promptly, and those using musl should investigate further.

sections.text: Negotiators from over 190 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for the COP31 climate summit. Ahead of the event, Turkey previewed the Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge, which encourages clean energy use, transparency, and e-waste management in data centres.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The pledge objectives are voluntary and non-prescriptive, creating no new obligations. Furthermore, the US, which has the most data centres, has no official delegates at the summit following a withdrawal from the global climate accord by Donald Trump.

timeline.text: Slight fall in carbon emissions from fossil fuels as Iran war drives renewables push

gist: Fossil fuel carbon emissions are forecast to drop slightly this year.
Higher oil and gas prices from the Iran war drove renewable uptake.
Total carbon emissions still rose due to increased deforestation and land use.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Carbon emissions from fossil fuels are expected to decrease slightly by about 0.4% this year. Oil and gas prices rose due to the war in Iran, prompting people to use less fuel and adopt electric vehicles. However, increased deforestation and land conversion led to higher total global carbon emissions overall.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Scientists warn that this year's reduction might be temporary and insufficient to prevent permanent global heating beyond 1.5C. Remaining carbon budgets are extremely limited, and global emissions must fall rapidly to avoid severe climate impacts.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Analysts note that permanent emission reductions require much greater investments in renewable energy and low-carbon technologies. It remains uncertain whether countries like China will experience sustained emission peaks or if future trends will rebound.

quotes.text: A drop in emissions in one year is not a peak, unless it is driven by structural change.
quotes.role: research professor at the Cicero Centre for International Climate Research

quotes.text: The picture from the Global Carbon Budget is a flatline, not a decline – a projected fall of just 0.4% in 2026, a figure that is unfortunately statistically indistinguishable from zero

timeline.text: Ukraine’s fiber-optic drones get squeezed by AI data center demand

gist: Ukraine's fiber-optic drones compete with global AI data centers for optical fiber.
Prices for fiber-optic material have multiplied due to intense demand and limited supply.
Ukrainian manufacturers are moving spooling in-house to improve quality and lower costs.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Fiber-optic drones have become common in Ukraine and Russia to bypass battlefield electronic jamming. However, importing optical fiber from China has become more costly because drone needs compete with global demand from AI data centers. Russia's massive purchases and tighter ties with China have given it a logistics advantage, while Ukraine faces higher costs, long transport routes, and supply shortages.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The competition for optical fiber strains supply chains and drives up prices significantly. Defective imported spools can cause drones and missions to fail, forcing Ukrainian manufacturers to adapt by bringing the spooling process in-house and performing strict quality control.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Manufacturers continue to navigate long delivery times, border logistics, and security risks. Companies must rely on specialized training, equipment configuration, and flight testing to maintain consistent production quality.

fivew: Ukrainian drone makers and representatives like Oleksiy from BlueBird Tech
Ukrainian drone manufacturers are adapting to optical fiber shortages driven by AI data center demand.
High global demand for optical fiber from AI data centers and Russia has squeezed supplies and raised prices.

quotes.text: If a fiber-optic spool has a defect, you can lose the drone, lose the mission, and lose the target.
That requires spooling equipment, people who understand the process, testing capabilities, and quality control.

gist: At least ten US refuelling planes left RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk on Monday.
The relocation followed a reported threat linked to Iran, according to media claims.
This marks the second time US military aircraft have been moved from a UK base recently.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Several US Air Force tankers departed from RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk on Monday and flew to other locations in Europe and Scotland. The US reportedly acted due to a perceived threat from Iran. Outlets differ on destinations, with some mentioning Germany, Spain and Scotland while another notes Germany, Italy and Scotland.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The redeployment highlights ongoing security concerns for large military assets stationed at British installations. It follows the earlier withdrawal of US bombers from RAF Fairford following an unrelated security incident. While Washington took a cautious approach, British officials noted no direct danger locally, though views on Iran's capabilities vary.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Authorities remain watchful while security threat levels at the affected airbases have been raised. Officials continue to review operational security and base protection measures in response to the developments.

gist: Delegates gather in Antalya for the Cop31 climate summit amidst severe challenges.
The 1.5C global temperature limit is set to be breached soon.
Organisers hope to adopt a goal to increase electricity's share in energy use.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Representatives from almost all nations met in Antalya for the annual Cop31 climate summit. Participants discussed the worsening climate situation, noting that the global temperature rise limit will likely be breached soon while emissions remain too high and wealthy nations lag on assistance commitments.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The summit tests whether international negotiation can still address global crises while geopolitical tensions, war, and inflation divert attention. Although major breakthroughs on eliminating fossil fuels are unlikely, successful implementation of existing goals remains crucial.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Delegates will continue talks over the two-week summit, with organisers confident about adopting a goal to boost the share of electricity in energy use.

gist: A drug user stole an ambulance containing an elderly patient and paramedic.
The thief was chased by police before fleeing on foot and hiding.
He was jailed for 21 months after admitting multiple offences.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Marshall Leese stole a running ambulance from outside a hospital in Stoke-on-Trent. A paramedic and an elderly patient were inside. Leese drove through red lights during a two-mile police chase before abandoning the vehicle at a petrol station on the A34. He hid nearby and was found by a police dog.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The court heard the elderly patient, who was on blood thinners for a head injury, would have died in a crash. The paramedic was terrified during the ordeal.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Leese was sentenced to 21 months in prison at Stoke-on-Trent Crown Court.

stories.standfirst: With 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and joined the fight against the occupying German forces.

articles.title: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
articles.standfirst: With 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and joined the fight against the occupying German forces.

timeline.text: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104

gist: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies at the age of 104.
She created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters during World War Two.
President Emmanuel Macron and others paid public tribute following her death.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Solange Alexandre, one of France's last World War Two resistance heroes, has died aged 104 at a nursing home in Le Mans. Starting as a courier in 1941, she later founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network and commanded about 30 men in sabotage and anti-German operations. She took part in the liberation of Tours and ended the war as a sub-lieutenant.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: She was a rare female commander of a resistance unit who served her country with distinction. President Emmanuel Macron paid tribute, stating that France will never forget her contribution.

quotes.text: She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you,
It is a great pleasure and a great honour. I am very proud – even if it is only a few weeks, or a few months, before I die.

gist: Brighton moved second in the Premier League after beating Brentford 2-0.
The Seagulls sit five points behind league leaders Arsenal after ten games.
Midfielder Pascal Gross has been central to Brighton's impressive early-season form.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Brighton defeated Brentford 2-0 at the Amex Stadium on Sunday to move into second place in the Premier League table. The victory marked their sixth win in seven matches, lifting them above Manchester City before the November international break.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Brighton's strong start puts them five points behind leaders Arsenal as the closest challengers. Underlying numbers show they have created many big chances and scored the most goals in the division, while keeping seven clean sheets.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Brighton head into the international break aiming to maintain their form for the remainder of the campaign. Meanwhile, Manchester City await the outcome of their appeal against Premier League financial rules breaches.

timeline.text: Another 1-0 for relentless Arsenal - but did Odegaard spare VAR blushes?

gist: Martin Odegaard scored the winning goal to secure a 1-0 victory for Arsenal.
A controversial VAR decision denied Arsenal a first-half penalty against Hull.
Arsenal went into the international break as the Premier League leaders.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Martin Odegaard scored a 72nd-minute goal to secure a 1-0 win for Arsenal against Hull. A penalty was initially expected for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz, but the referee pivoted to an offside decision after a VAR review.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident highlighted ongoing confusion and debate surrounding VAR interpretations of fouls versus offside offences. Arsenal secured three points to remain Premier League leaders, though their attack continues to lack fluency.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Arsenal enter the international break at the top of the table as they aim to improve their attacking efficiency and defend their league crown.

fivew: Arsenal secured a 1-0 victory with a goal from Martin Odegaard.
To remain Premier League leaders going into the international break.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Everton beat Coventry 3-1 after goals from Thierno Barry and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall following Yann Gboho's opener. Coventry manager Frank Lampard questioned three major decisions going against his side, including a penalty appeal for hair pulling.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Lampard felt decisions regarding a hair pull, a challenge on Taiwo Awoniyi and a potential handball by Barry changed the game. Everton boss David Moyes disagreed over the handball and criticised the hair pull rule.

fivew: Coventry lost 3-1 to Everton after controversial refereeing and VAR decisions.

gist: Brighton climbed to second in the Premier League after beating Brentford 2-0.
The Seagulls sit five points behind league leaders Arsenal after ten matches.
Midfielder Pascal Gross downplayed any suggestions that his side are in a title race.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Brighton defeated Brentford 2-0 at the Amex Stadium on Sunday afternoon. The victory lifted the Seagulls into second place in the Premier League, moving them above Manchester City before the November international break.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Brighton have won seven of their opening ten matches, establishing themselves as the closest challengers to league leaders Arsenal with a five-point gap. Their strong underlying numbers and defensive record suggest they could maintain this early-season form.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Brighton head into the international break aiming to maintain their momentum for the remainder of the campaign, while awaiting the return of injured players like Kaoru Mitoma.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester City fell to a 3-1 defeat against Forest at the City Ground, marking their third consecutive Premier League loss. Defensive blunders allowed Jair Cunha and Liam Delap to score. A strike from Rayan Cherki gave City brief hope, but they could not turn the match around.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The defeat leaves City six points behind the champions after 10 games, a position from which few teams have recovered to win the title. Manager Enzo Maresca faces growing pressure regarding defensive vulnerabilities, individual errors, and squad trust during the international break.

gist: Manchester United drew four-all with Aston Villa after scoring a stoppage-time equaliser.
Manager Michael Carrick remains in his position despite United dropping into the relegation zone.
Fans protested against club owners and ticket prices amid poor league form.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester United drew four-all against Aston Villa in an eight-goal thriller at Old Trafford. United fought back twice from two goals down, securing a point with a ninety-sixth-minute equaliser from Patrick Dorgu. The result left United in eighteenth place in the relegation zone during the international break.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: United are in their lowest league position for forty years after playing at least ten matches, having failed to win a league game since August. The poor form has intensified pressure on manager Michael Carrick and sparked unprecedented fan protests against ticket prices and club ownership.
